requirements.adequate_response: Distinguish averages from individuals and group composition; give a mechanism for each pairing (gender, skill, ownership sector, agriculture/manufacturing/services).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q19 ER lists seniority, private (higher)/public (lower), regional, bonus/overtime, experience, responsibility; 2022 P1 (d) as above; 2022 P1 Q (c) women self-employment/gender wage inequality extract.
requirements.gap: No card on within-occupation pay differences (seniority, experience, location, bonus). Public sector pay claims are unverified.
requirements.repetition: J scarce-skill mechanism repeated across sector labels (J-007, J-012, J-015).
requirements.why: J pairs each printed grouping (male/female, skilled, private/public, agriculture, manufacturing, service) with a mechanism card; V mostly defines terms (013-016).

requirements.syllabus_text: analyse and discuss changes in earnings over time between occupations and between economic sectors
requirements.demand: Analyse/discuss: explain why relative earnings change and interpret nominal v real change.
requirements.adequate_response: Use demand/supply changes, productivity, bargaining; compute real change from a price index; avoid single-cause claims.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q10 define real income (ER: most defined disposable income); 2022 P1 Q13 real disposable income N$5,000 at 3.5% inflation = N$4,825; 2023 P2 real income per capita (ER: only 1 mark).
requirements.gap: No card defines real income; no card gives the exam's real income method (income minus inflation% x income = N$4,825 vs exact deflation N$4,831); no occupational/sector time-series data card.
requirements.why: V gives nominal/real vocabulary and exam-evidenced misconception; J gives growth-gap mechanism (J-017) and supply-response (J-016).

requirements.syllabus_text: explain economic rent and transfer earnings
requirements.demand: Explain/apply: separate reward into minimum and excess and use a stated figure.
requirements.adequate_response: Define both, split a stated reward, and avoid reversing them; optional diagram (area between supply curve and wage).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P2 4(b) 7 marks soccer player N$1,000 willing N$800: TE N$800, rent N$200; ER 'Poorly answered. Majority lack subject knowledge'; graph optional (+2).
requirements.gap: No diagram card showing rent as the area between wage and supply curve.
requirements.why: Definitions V-017/018, distinction and numeric split J-019/020, reversal MISCON V-020.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe how and why different income groups have different expenditure patterns (spending, saving, borrowing)
requirements.demand: Describe and explain (understand/apply): compare amounts and shares for different incomes and give reasons.
requirements.adequate_response: Use share = spending/income; explain why low-income households spend more of income on essentials, save less, borrow for emergencies with limited access.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 (d) 'savings and spending patterns change for different groups and income levels over a career'; 2022 P2 (c) factors determining spending.
requirements.gap: No card on factors determining spending (disposable income, wealth, expectations) or life-cycle pattern.
requirements.why: J gives the why for spending, saving and borrowing; V mostly defines.

requirements.syllabus_text: analyse the different motives for spending, saving and borrowing
requirements.demand: Analyse: identify and develop motives for each of the three behaviours.
requirements.adequate_response: Name spending motives (necessity, want), saving motives (emergency, planned purchase, interest), borrowing motives (bridge, urgent need).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P2 (c) factors for spending of a soccer player; 2023 P2 (b) interest rate fall on savings of different individuals.
requirements.gap: No want-driven spending motive card (status, advertising); no retirement/education saving motive card.
requirements.why: J has separate motive cards for all three; V has only precautionary saving and one borrowing card.

requirements.syllabus_text: analyse and discuss changes in patterns of expenditure between groups and over a period of time
requirements.demand: Analyse/discuss: explain how price, interest, income changes alter patterns.
requirements.adequate_response: Compare shares over time, effect of price rises on fixed income, interest effects on saving and borrowing, group differences in response.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 (d) career pattern; 2023 P2 (b) interest rates; 2022 P2 (c) inflation, interest, taxes on spending.
requirements.gap: No card on inflation effect on spending/saving; no life-cycle card; no tax or credit availability changes.
requirements.why: V-009 time-share; J-016/017 price and interest responses.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe and analyse the principle of profit maximisation as a goal
requirements.demand: Describe/analyse: define; distinguish highest profit from highest revenue/output; apply TR-TC and MC=MR.
requirements.adequate_response: State profit = TR-TC; maximum where MC = MR; compare options by profit not revenue.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 Q4(a) 3 marks describe profit maximisation (MC = MR; TR-TC); 2022 P2 3(c) 7 marks 'whether a firm should always maximise profit' (ER: majority scored 1 mark stating MR = MC; ER notes 'could not give the difference between TC and TR'); 2023 P2 Q2(a) link productivity/maximum profits (6).
requirements.gap: Neither bank has an MR/MC table card; J never states MC = MR; V states it only in the definition. No card on goals other than profit (2022 P2 3(c)).
requirements.repetition: J uses the same 10/20/30 batch data in J-001, J-008, J-P01.
requirements.why: V-001 (revised) states the rule; J-008/J-P01 provide the misconception and the calculation.

requirements.demand: Define: goods and services created to satisfy wants.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 Q4(b) production v productivity (ER: learners did not mention goods/services).
requirements.why: V-004 is more complete and marked at 2.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe what determines the demand for factors of production
requirements.demand: Describe: derived demand; contribution (productivity); price of factor and of substitutes/complements.
requirements.adequate_response: Explain demand for labour/capital as derived from product demand and productivity.
requirements.exam_evidence: No direct item found; 2022 P1 Q15 productivity of capital goods (ER: poorly answered, learners did not define capital goods).
requirements.gap: No card on factor price changes, relative factor prices, marginal revenue product (V notes mention MRP; no card), or capital goods definition.

requirements.syllabus_text: analyse particular situations to show the effects of substituting one factor for another
requirements.demand: Analyse: compare factor combinations for cost, output and employment.
requirements.adequate_response: Compute profit under alternative methods, note full costs, utilisation, effects on workers.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P2 and 2022 ER mention machinery/capital intensity; 2022 P1 Q15 'Some learners described capital intensive'.
requirements.gap: No card on a change in relative factor price causing substitution; no capital-/labour-intensive definition card.
requirements.why: J quantifies; V states benefit/limit qualitatively.

requirements.demand: Explain/understand: output per unit of input; differ from production.
requirements.adequate_response: Give formula and distinguish production from productivity.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q13 formula (2); 2021 P2 Q4(b) production v productivity (ER: fairly well answered, mentioned output measured against input); 2022 P1 Q15 productivity of capital goods (3).

requirements.adequate_response: Calculate and interpret productivity from figures.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q13 write the formula (2); 2022 P1 Q15 output per hour.
requirements.why: J-003 marks formula and result; V-006 adds percentage interpretation.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss how productivity can be improved
requirements.demand: Discuss: weigh methods (training, equipment, layout, incentives).
requirements.adequate_response: Explain two or more methods and the mechanism for each.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q14 list two ways (1 mark); 2021 P2 Q4(c) 7 marks 'how a company might improve production' (training, better machines, combine factors, division of labour, participation, profit sharing; ER: learners listed without explaining).
requirements.gap: No card on machinery/technology, motivation/incentive (profit sharing, piece rate), division of labour, health/education as ways to raise productivity.
requirements.why: V-009 and V-010 plus J-006 bottleneck.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain the effect of Information Technology on productivity
requirements.adequate_response: Give mechanism and a risk (training, downtime).
requirements.exam_evidence: No IT-specific past-paper question found in extracts.
requirements.why: V cards require the learner to supply conditions.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss the effects of HIV and AIDS on productivity
requirements.demand: Discuss: link illness/absence/stigma to output and cost, without status inference.
requirements.adequate_response: State effects (absenteeism, lower output, higher costs, reduced labour supply, discrimination) and note support/treatment.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q14 ways to protect workers with HIV/AIDS; 2022 P1 Q16 two disadvantages (ER: absenteeism, low productivity, increased costs, reduced supply of labour, discrimination); 2023 P2 Q2(b) negative influence on productivity and profit (6).
requirements.gap: Neither bank states the exam's disadvantages list or worker-protection measures; J-010 is mistagged.
requirements.why: V states the definition and exam-aligned absence effect; J-009/J-010 over-scaffolded.
